title: Analysis  of Floral Trait Diversity and Its Correlation with Fertility in Hibiscus Syriacus Cultivars
content: Hibiscus syriacus L. is a landscape plant with ornamental, economic, and ecological value. However, the low natural fruit-setting rate observed in most cultivars significantly hinders its cross-breeding, germplasm innovation, and large-scale application. In this study, we analysed 20 cultivars to identify the key floral traits associated with H. syriacus fertility. Fifty floral phenotypic and pollen morphological indicators were systematically quantified, fruit-setting and pollen vitality rates were recorded, and insect foraging behaviours were observed to assess the diversity of floral characteristics and their correlation with fertility. The results showed that notable variations in floral phenotype and pollen morphology exist among the studied cultivars. Pollen grains were characterised by spinous ornamentation, with notable differences in grain size, spine morphology, and surface wrinkling. Correlation analysis identified 9 core floral and palynological indicators that are highly associated with H. syriacus fertility. These comprise five floral phenotypic variables, such as pistil length (PL2) and heart length (HL), and four microscopic palynological features, including thorn curvature (TC) and spine number (TN). In this study, we established a phenotypic and palynological framework for understanding fruit-setting in H. syriacus. These 9 core metrics have the potential to serve as morphological markers for the rapid evaluation of hybrid parents, thereby providing a scientific basis for genetic improvement, cultivar breeding, and the industrial expansion of this species.
